title: UBS surges Bitcoin call options 24-fold while trimming direct holdings in Q2 2026
dek: UBS increased call option exposure on BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) to 1.95 million underlying shares (up from 80,000), a 24-fold jump, while direct IBIT holdings rose 12% to 407,890 shares as of June 30, 2026. The bank cut put option exposure roughly in half, shifting its net posture more bullish.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: UBS call option exposure on IBIT reached 1.95 million underlying shares in Q2 2026, a 24-fold increase from Q1, per CoinDesk's analysis of the bank's regulatory filings.
bottom_line: UBS increases IBIT holdings 12% to 407K shares and call options 24x; major institutional bank deepening crypto positions with concrete holding data.
body: UBS increased its call option exposure on BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) to 1.95 million underlying shares as of June 30, 2026, up from 80,000 shares three months earlier, a 24-fold increase, according to CoinDesk's analysis of the bank's regulatory filings released August 15. The move represents a significant shift in how the $7 trillion Swiss bank is positioning itself toward Bitcoin, though the filing leaves the strength of that conviction ambiguous.

UBS's direct IBIT holdings also rose, climbing to 407,890 shares worth approximately $13.6 million, a 12 percent increase from 364,371 shares held at the end of Q1 2026. However, those direct holdings remain below the 548,614 shares the bank held at the end of 2025, meaning UBS has trimmed its outright exposure over the first half of the year even as it has ramped up leveraged call positions.

On the downside, UBS cut its put option exposure to 143,300 underlying shares as of June 30, down roughly 53 percent from 303,300 at the end of March. The reduction in puts, paired with the surge in calls, tilts UBS's net options posture more bullish. Yet the filing contains no strike prices or expiration dates for either the calls or puts, leaving independent analysts unable to determine whether these options are deeply out of the money, about to expire, or positioned for near-term moves.

Context for the move came earlier in 2026, when UBS began preparing to offer select private banking clients in Switzerland access to Bitcoin and Ether trading. Whether the options increase reflects client-driven demand, proprietary trading bets by the bank, or dealer hedging on behalf of other counterparties remains unconfirmed. The filing itself does not disclose the bank's rationale.

The bear case rests on three gaps in transparency. First, without strike prices and expirations, the net directional exposure cannot be independently assessed: a 1.95 million share position could be a far out-of-the-money hedge expiring in weeks, or a deep in-the-money bullish bet maturing next year. Second, the decline in direct IBIT holdings from year-end suggests UBS may be using options as a lower-capital way to maintain exposure while reducing cash outlay. Third, the filing leaves entirely unclear whether the bank is betting its own capital or facilitating client positions.

The Bottom Line: UBS's options surge signals institutional interest in Bitcoin leveraged exposure, but the absence of strike data and the persistent decline in direct holdings from prior year-end levels suggest the narrative of "deepening Bitcoin conviction" may be incomplete. Watch for follow-on disclosures that reveal strike prices, expirations, and the client-versus-proprietary split; those details will determine whether this is conviction or capital efficiency.
